bugs.summary: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization Resource ids (groupResource.getId()) instead of group ids, and passes that resource id to hasPermission which looks resources up by name (= group id); callers then filter users by these ids as group ids, so an admin granted view-members gets user counts/lists for a non-existent group set.
bugs.evidence: GroupPermissionsV2.java:121-123 iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) then granted.add(groupResource.getId()). hasPermission at :141 does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-121 names per-group resources by resolveGroup (:181-185 returns group.getId()), so resource name = group id, resource id = generated authz id; findByName(resourceId) is null and falls back to the all-groups resource. Consumers treat the result as group ids: UsersResource.java:398/425/430/448 and BruteForceUsersResource.java:147 pass it to session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds); contract UserCountMethodsProvider.java:55 '@param groupIds set of groups IDs, the returned user needs to belong to at least one of them'; JpaUserProvider.java:599-607 binds them to the userCountInGroups query. Resource ids never match group ids, so the filter matches no users. Upstream later removed this method (now throws UnsupportedOperationException in fgap/GroupPermissionsV2). Also, per-group resources are created untyped (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:119 `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, ...)` with no setType; only the all-resource 'Groups' gets setType at :274), so findByType returns just the all-groups resource: an all-groups view-members grant yields that resource's id (search finds no users, count 0) and per-group grants are never iterated (JpaUserProvider.java:600-602 returns 0 for the empty set).

bugs.summary: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no group) accepts the VIEW scope, so an admin granted only view on all groups passes auth.groups().requireManage() and can create top-level groups or move groups to the top level.
bugs.evidence: GroupPermissionsV2.java:65-71 `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, while canManage(group) at :74-80 checks only MANAGE. GroupsResource.java:181 addTopLevelGroup calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, which creates or reparents groups. Upstream main fgap/GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() checks only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`. Golden comment.
